These arguments use the nonempty *site* of a rule; a blank port block in the test arity is simply labelled by the identity.

In the universal cover each lift of the attaching piece contributes a single copy of $H_{*-(k-1)}(Z)$, indexed by the deck group. Any lift of $p$ takes one whole such copy isomorphically to one copy downstairs in the cover of $E_N$: on the simply connected attaching piece it is the identity on $Z$ and on $P$, with only the choice of lift left. For $F_D$ the positive-side covering calculation in Response 99 takes a whole copy isomorphically to a single copy. Explicitly, the separated spatial cube fixes a bottom generator up to a single deck translate. Capping with pullbacks of source classes forces the higher images into that same copy, because those classes restrict onto $H^*(Z)$. Projection to ordinary relative homology then gives the isomorphism on that copy. Lifting the naturality square with $p$ shows that $F_N$ does the same on at least one copy. A homotopy in that square changes only the deck translation. Since $F_N$ already induces a deck group isomorphism, equivariance now gives an isomorphism on the entire lifted relative homology. The equivalence on $L$ also compares its pulled-back covers. The lifted pair sequence and simply connected Whitehead prove the equivalence on $E_N$. This argument does not require $p$ to be an equivalence on total arrow spaces.

### The planar pure strata

At $n=2$ we need a weak equivalence on the pure strata themselves. The comparison gives self-maps of ordered planar configuration spaces coherent for all partial bijections. We show that **any** such endomorphism is an equivalence. Passage to the homotopy quotient by $S_m$ gives an endomorphism $f_m$ of the full braid group $B_m$ over its permutation quotient, up to basepoint transport. In particular its image for $m\ge5$ is noncyclic. The pure subgroup is $P_m$. On $H_1(P_m)=\mathbb Z^{M}$, $M=\binom m2$, forgetting down to each pair reads its linking number. Thus the restriction acts by $e$ times the identity for the degree $e$ of the two-name map. Orevkov's Theorem 1.6 gives $f_m$ as a transvection of an automorphism $g_m$. The centre is generated by the full twist, which is pure, so $g_m$ preserves $P_m$ in both directions. A pure pair generator has full-braid exponent two, and the full twist has linking number one on every pair. For an integer $t$ the matrix of $g_m$ on $H_1(P_m)$ is consequently $e\,\mathrm{id}-2t\,\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}$. Its determinant $e^{M-1}(e-2tM)$ is a unit. This forces $e=\pm1$ and $t=0$. The transvection is trivial, so $f_m$ restricts to an automorphism on the pure subgroup. [Orevkov, Theorem 1.6 and Lemma 2.1](https://afst.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/afst.1763.pdf)

In lower arities forget from five or more names. Forgetting is onto on pure braid groups by the configuration fibration with connected fibre. Naturality therefore gives surjectivity of the smaller endomorphism. Each $P_m$ is Hopfian: it is finitely generated and residually finite by the faithful Artin representation into automorphisms of a finite-rank free group. For the latter residual finiteness, distinguish the image of a changed free word in a finite characteristic quotient, taking the intersection of the finitely many subgroups of bounded index. The ordered planar spaces are aspherical, so the maps are equivalences in all arities, including the empty and singleton configurations. [Configuration spaces and braid actions](#researcher-response-82)

### Coherent cubes in the plane

For an independent interval of any of these diagrams let $T_C$ be the **space of coherent Boolean cubes**, the core of the functor category of sections of $C\to[1]^B$. A site configuration gives its characteristic cube, hence a map $h_C:Z\to T_C$. In the space-enriched cubical resolution this is the characteristic functor on each parameter, including the compositional faces of its permutohedron. In particular $p h_D=h_N$ and $q h_D=h_U$ up to the canonical equivalences. For $U$, evaluation at the initial corner is an equivalence $T_U\to Z$: a section is a map from the contractible cube category to the groupoid $Z$. The map $h_U$ is an inverse. By naturality of evaluation and the pure-stratum result, $F_U$ induces an equivalence on $T_U$.

For $D$, $h_D$ identifies $Z$ with the **entire component of its separated cube** in $T_D$. To prove this, every event in this interval has both ports nonempty, and every subinterval has the positive planar schedule calculation of Response 82. Hence all its fixed-object homs are homotopy discrete. This applies also to the identity strata, since their configuration groupoids are 1-types. The interval category is equivalent over the cuts to its ordinary homotopy category. Thus the component of a cube in $T_D$ is the classifying space of its group of natural automorphisms. We compute this group at the cube formed at a fixed separated site configuration. A natural automorphism gives one pure braid at each corner. Along an edge its two corner braids must be the input and output expansions of a common site braid. Indeed the varying-end one-use arrow space is the ordered site configuration, and its fundamental group gives exactly the natural automorphisms of that arrow. The two expansion maps on pure groups are injective since a representative port from each block retracts the expansion. Starting from the initial corner braid its value at every other corner is therefore forced by the edge conditions.

At the initial corner the braid must lie in every subgroup obtained by cabling the input block of one event, with all other live wires treated individually. Their intersection is the subgroup cabling all the input blocks at once. To check this at the common expanded base configuration, retain a representative of each chosen block and reinsert its fixed port configuration. For disjoint blocks these based idempotents commute by operad substitution in the complete graph model; each image is exactly the corresponding cabling subgroup. The image of their product is their intersection and is the simultaneous cabling subgroup. Every member of it comes from a unique braid in $\pi_1 Z$, and varying the sites by that braid gives a natural automorphism on the *entire* cube. Uniqueness from the edges proves the claim on automorphism groups. Both spaces are connected 1-types on these components, proving the assertion about $h_D$. [Planar injectivity and the commuting cluster retractions](#researcher-response-82)

The separated cube and its image under $F_D$ belong to the same component of $T_D$. Here it matters that a **single coherent cube**, rather than separate comparisons on its edges, was tested in Response 99. Specialize its raw spatial arity with one event in each column and one edge per stationary wire. The raw and interpreted specializations factor through the constraint imposing the prescribed exterior order between these blocks. This remains true with the incident-wire and singleton marks: within a generic column the port edges are internal, and separations between distinct columns have the last spatial level throughout. The constrained category is equivalent over the Boolean cuts to the product of the individual block categories. In the factor for an event $b$, a section cube sends every edge in directions other than $b$ to an equivalence, as it stays in one pure stratum there. Localizing those directions in $[1]^B$ gives $[1]$ up to equivalence: it is the projection onto $b$, with contractible groupoid completions of the other interval factors. Consequently the space of section cubes in that factor is the space of varying-end arrows making its one transition, equivalent to its contractible one-site space. A stationary singleton contributes a contractible groupoid. The entire constrained section space is therefore contractible, which supplies a path of coherent cubes over the cuts between the two specializations. [Separated arity test, including its composition maps](#researcher-response-99)

We now have $F_D h_D\simeq h_D A$ for some self-map $A$ of $Z$, since $h_D$ is an equivalence onto that component. Project with $q$. As $h_U$ and the induced endomorphism of $T_U$ are equivalences, $A$ is an equivalence. Project instead with $p$ to get
$$
                         F_N h_N\simeq h_N A\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Map}(Z,T_N).
$$
No asphericity of the unpadded arrow spaces is needed. For clarity on how this compares their attachment, every coherent cube induces a map from the factorization pair of the *bare* Boolean category to the pair $(E_N,L_N)$ by postcomposition. The bare pair is modeled by $(P,\partial P)$ using the ordered-refinement resolution. Applied to $h_N$ this gives the characteristic family of pairs, whose boundary attaches to $L_N$ by composing at the chosen intermediate cuts. The resulting square with top row $Z\times\partial P\to Z\times P$ and bottom row $L_N\to E_N$ is homotopy cocartesian by the schedule calculation. Postcomposition acts on this whole square. The displayed homotopy of cube families identifies its action on the characteristic family with $A$ times the identity of the bare pair, including the homotopy on the attaching boundary. Hence the maps on the two top entries are equivalences and, by proper-interval induction, so is the map on $L_N$. The homotopy pushout gives an equivalence on $E_N$, including when $L_N$ is disconnected or empty. The dependent intervals use $L_N\simeq E_N$ exactly as above. This completes the planar induction.

In all ranks the pure strata and total arrow spaces have been compared by equivalences over the same endpoints. Taking the homotopy fibres therefore compares the specified raw homs. An insertion filler there gives a filler after $F_N$ and hence a raw filler at the original named faces by the globe test. Folding the lifts yields the required raw term in the given computad. In degree $n+1$ the surface history itself has a raw realization by connectedness of the pure components; the smaller degrees are the pure-skeleton cases. ∎

**A planar old type distinguished by the result.** Take two distinct stationary $2$-scalars and a $3$-generator $d$ with both port blocks empty. For one use of $d$ the moving-end space is $\operatorname{Conf}_2(3)$; both end maps forget its site. At the same fixed two-wire configuration the raw arrow space is equivalent to $(\mathbb R^2\setminus\{s,t\})\times\Omega\operatorname{Conf}_2(2)$. Indeed the first endpoint path takes the homotopy fibre of the forgetful configuration fibration, and concatenation of the two endpoint paths gives the independent loop at the fixed configuration. Choose the arrow with the site in the complement and with constant endpoint paths. Pushing that site around each of the two wires yields two raw $4$-loops at this arrow by the fixed-boundary globe comparison. Their commutator and its constant loop give parallel old $4$-faces. The resulting $5$-type is uninhabited under insertion: the commutator is nontrivial in the free group on the two meridians, and the theorem reflects any filler. Each projection to two of the three particles kills the commutator. Thus even an obstruction invisible in every pair projection survives conversion in this context. The unrestricted classification in Q1, and Q2 for arbitrary finite contexts, still require other arguments.

**Validation.** For two events with zero, one or two real ports on each side and one bypass wire, direct calculation verified 1,944 commuting projection/endpoint faces and 162 identifications of the full batch. Using the faithful Artin action on 724 pure braid words, 96 elements belonged to both individual cluster groups; these and precisely these were fixed by the simultaneous cabling retraction. The Artin action also detects the three-strand point-pushing commutator and verifies all three trivial pair projections. For ranks two, three and four Rice's checker accepted the two raw unit fittings around each of a birth, a death and a portless event and their full three-event hexagon at the padded types. In insertion mode it also checked definitional agreement of that whole fitted hexagon with the original, and rejected changing the portless event to a distinct parallel one. These give 12 typed checker runs. Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_port_erasure.py --catt-strict /path/to/catt-strict` in the environment of Response 104. [Port projections, planar braid calculations and typed cubes](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_port_erasure.py)

## Researcher Response 109

**A characteristic Gray tensor of intervals and directed 2-globes has a surface reverse exactly when two interval factors are consecutive.** Take its unfolded spatial arity, a binary surface containing $I$, and local total rank $D\ge2$. The question is at the old boundary reversing the native top tensor. In particular $I\otimes P\otimes I$, where $P$ is a 2-globe, has no surface reverse, whereas $I\otimes I\otimes P$ does. Here the letter $I$ in a displayed tensor denotes an interval. When there are no consecutive intervals, **every** old comparison of global degree $D+1$ in this characteristic fixed hom reflects the full binary surface. This settles the bare mixed top questions underlying the two different bounds of Response 92.

Let $K_i$ be the augmented directed chain complex of the interval or the 2-globe in column $i$. Use rational chains, with the nonnegative rational cones. In each spatial subinterval take the tensor of its columns. Impose the following tensor ideal of chain relations: kill each elementary square of two edge factors with only vertex factors between them, and kill its boundary. Tensor these relations with arbitrary factors outside the indicated subinterval on either side. The resulting subspaces are closed under the differential by the Leibniz rule. Give each quotient the image positive cone. These complexes compose by concatenating tensors, with the tensor unit at each object and empty homs in the backward direction after realization. The chain quotients here are used as a *model* and require no identification of the actual surface syntax with a linear quotient.

We verify that every positive cycle of positive rank in these quotients is zero. Separate basis words by the exact set $J$ of columns carrying a degree-two polygon. The relations are homogeneous for $J$: a killed square or its boundary has no polygon in its span, and the outside factors are unchanged. Between the columns in $J$, including both end gaps, are blocks containing only vertices and edges. In such a block any term containing two or more edges vanishes by taking two consecutive active edges. In block rank one the relations are precisely the boundaries of the elementary squares, identifying the two route chains around a rectangle. In rank zero there are no relations. Indeed a tensored square boundary with an additional outside edge in the same block has zero terms already. Consequently a $J$-sector is the tensor of these rank-zero-and-one blocks, interleaved with the specified polygon factors. The augmentation on block vertices, the total count of block edges, and the count of a specified phase edge of a specified column independent of its other vertex coordinates respect the required block relations. In particular the total sum of coefficients on any fixed set of active blocks is well defined. A nonnegative representative with any surviving basis word has a nonzero image.

Suppose there is a nonzero positive cycle of rank $d$. Choose a nonzero sector with the largest number of polygons. Write $t=d-2|J|$. If $t>0$, keep $t$ blocks simultaneously carrying one edge each in some positive term and augment the other blocks. In this sector the differential preserving $J$ acts on the block factors only. No larger sector contributes, and a different sector of the same cardinality cannot contribute. On the component dropping the edge of the first selected block, evaluate the sum of the vertex bits in that block, the edge counts in the other selected blocks and the augmentations elsewhere. Every block edge increases the sum of vertex bits by one. Thus the evaluation of the differential is strictly positive up to a single common sign. If $t=0$, choose a polygon $j\in J$ and inspect the sector $J\setminus\{j\}$ of the differential. Count the upper phase edge of column $j$ in its block and augment all other vertex blocks. Dropping $j$ contributes once per term of the chosen sector, with a common sign. Dropping a different polygon into this sector contributes zero to that particular edge count. A preserving differential from a chain already in $J\setminus\{j\}$ acts on two different edge blocks: to contribute the marked edge it must differentiate the other block, whose endpoint difference augments to zero. These exhaust the possible terms. This again contradicts the cycle condition.

Apply Steiner's $\nu$ to these quotient complexes. The resulting homs compose by strict functors from their lax Gray tensors: the right adjoint $\nu$ is lax monoidal, since $\lambda$ takes the Gray tensor to the chain tensor. For the latter identification one can check the strong Steiner charts and extend by density and separate preservation of colimits. Use ordinary underlying abelian groups of the rational complexes, with multiplication of rational coefficients for the spatial pairing. This gives a strict Gray-enriched interpretation. A local endomorphism of positive rank must be an identity because its top chain is a positive cycle. Any square on two local arrows goes to an identity: the chain pairing on two positive 1-chains is a sum of the killed elementary squares. The word and head criterion of Response 19 therefore gives a model of the full binary surface, and hence of every smaller binary surface. It applies also to arbitrary labelled arrows in these quotient homs, since their top chains have positive representatives. [Strict word and head criterion](#researcher-response-19) · [Steiner's monoidal construction and adjunction](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403237)

In the full chart the unique top chain generator $e$ has polygons exactly in the 2-globe slots. It survives precisely when every intervening block, including the two end blocks, has at most one interval. Its boundary then survives by the positive-cycle calculation. Since the top cone lies on a single ray, a cell reversing its boundary in this model would need coefficient $-1$. More generally the original chart is augmented-contractible and concentrated through rank $D$. For parallel tableaux of rank $D-1$ the integral difference of top faces has the form $k\partial e$ for a unique integer $k$ (in the rank-one-face case use their equal endpoints). A surface filler in the surviving case forces $k\ge0$ by the same ray test. Then $ke$ itself gives the strict filler at these faces, and the arity comparison gives a raw filler at the original writings. If two interval factors are consecutive, Response 92 gives the surface reverse by specializing their square to the identity; for a sole pair this is the defining interchange conversion. The raw reverse of the characteristic top is absent by the original nonzero boundary. [Square degeneration](#researcher-response-92) · [Arity comparison](#researcher-response-8)

**Reproduction.** Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_square_quotient_chains.py` with islpy. The solver explicitly constructs the ideal subspaces, reduces all tensor differentials, and independently computes the linear hull of each nonnegative cycle cone in local ranks at least three. It checks that those cycles are already relations. All 28 interval/polygon words of lengths two through four agree with the consecutive-interval criterion, through local rank eight. Passing `IPIPI` tests two separated polygons in a rank-seven chart. [Exact quotient-chain solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_square_quotient_chains.py)

## Researcher Response 110

**For every weighted globular interval of Response 92, the exact failing degrees above three are determined except possibly global degree six.** For a surface containing interchange the failures include $4,\ldots,M+1$ as there, and **no degree outside this list other than six can fail**. The exception needs $W=6$, $M=4$ and a maximum reversed triple with all three slots updated. Degree six reflects there too whenever each maximum-weight triple has at most two updates per slot. There is a reproducible integer-tableau test for additional finite update counts. A triangle-free interval still reflects throughout by Response 91.

Use the common ordinary value with occurrences unfolded. Let $R$ order the slots by the order common to the initial and final temporal shuffle. In the ordinary cubical complex of its ideals, the active coordinates form an enabled antichain; the completed coordinates form the cut before them. In each active coordinate use the slot complex with its parallel phase edges and its directed 2-cells between successive phases. Glue these products at their polar vertices. This is a face-closed subbasis of the tensor of the column path complexes, with the slots of each column in their prescribed order. Every chart of a reading between the two shuffles lies in it: a native interval exchange changes a given pair in only one direction, so every intermediate shuffle preserves each common ordering, and private updates preserve the slot order. Completing a contextual generator by its outside readings gives its enabled antichain. Conversely a nonnegative chain in this subbasis with the prescribed tableau boundary is a strict filler in the full tensor. The subcomplex is integrally contractible: retract each phase disk to its first interval edge relative to the two poles, compatibly in all products. The remaining ideal cubes retract by moving a maximal slot coordinate to zero, then repeating. A completed maximal slot can retreat with all other active coordinates fixed since none is its successor or an unfinished predecessor. Consequently for parallel $(d-1)$-faces in our ranks there is an integral particular $d$-chain $z_0$ *in the interval* with the prescribed boundary. [Unfolded weighted interval](#researcher-response-92) · [Ideal complex](#researcher-response-93)

The chain model of Response 109 works for any number of successive private updates per slot. In the sector proof specify the precise update in each polygon slot. The degree-one counting functional detecting a dropped update now counts every phase at or beyond its output phase on the chosen axis. It changes by one on that update and by zero on every other update of that slot. The rest of the positive-cycle proof is unchanged. We can therefore use its quotient on the projections that keep one reversed clique of slots and all their phases.

If there is a reversed triple, then $W-M\le2$. A maximum clique with at least three slots loses at most two by forcing its adjacent pair; a smaller maximum has weight at most four and $M\ge3$. When $M<W$, no maximum clique has two consecutive bare intervals. In local rank $W$ each possible atom has its own maximum clique and its outside stationary cut is forced, as in Response 92. Project onto that clique. In the projected tensor the top basis consists of one box choice in each updated slot and the edge in each bare slot. Its differential is injective **even after the square quotient**. If there is a bare slot, restrict to the sector with all the chosen boxes still present and differentiate that particular interval. Its block has just the one axis; its vertex difference survives and reads the coefficient for those particular boxes. If every slot is updated, the component differentiating one chosen column has the full phase-edge basis there and all other columns at their boxes. No square relation acts there; the successive phase differences of that column are independent. The quotient top cone still has nonnegative basis coefficients. A surface witness thus forces each projected coefficient of $z_0$ nonnegative. All coefficients are tested, which gives the raw filler at local rank $W$. When $M=W-1$ this already closes the entire gap.

Suppose $W=M+2$. Every maximum clique consists entirely of updated slots: a bare member and one neighbour would lose at most one. A maximum with fewer than three slots is excluded by $M\ge3$. At local rank $d=W-1$, possible atoms either use all slots of a weight-$W$ clique $C$, with just one box replaced by a phase edge, or use all slots at their full weights in a weight-$d$ clique $S$. Every such $S$ is maximal: adding a slot would give a weight-$W$ clique with a bare member. It has no consecutive bare slots, since that would give $M\ge d$. The top projection argument for $S$ already gives nonnegativity there. For each $C$, the projection to it isolates precisely the rank-$d$ coefficients with support $C$: even omitting one of its slots drops the possible weight to $W-2$. Its outside cut is again unique. Adjusting $z_0$ by a boundary of a top chain on $C$ changes only these coefficients since differentiating a polygon leaves a phase edge in that same slot. We can therefore choose those adjustments independently, and glue them to the coefficients for $S$.

**The calculation one rank below the top.** Write $r=|C|$, so $W=2r$. In this all-polygon tensor no rank-$d$ cell is killed and the ideal in rank $d-1$ is exactly the span of words with two phase edges in *adjacent* slots and boxes everywhere else. A tensored boundary-of-square relation at this rank would have a killed rank-$d$ word above it, of which there are none. Consider a signed cycle $y$ in this span. Differentiating an edge to its vertex difference shows that the coefficients of each term family with its two edge slots fixed separately have zero phase sum in each of those slots: the component with one vertex, one edge and boxes elsewhere sees just that family. The phase differences $B_i^j=\partial P_i^j$ of the successive boxes form a basis of the zero-sum phase subspace. Expand in these bases at the edge slots. For each tuple of box indices separately one obtains coefficients $u_{ij}$ on words with two $B$'s instead of boxes, zero for nonconsecutive $i,j$. The boundary equations are precisely
$$
            u_{ij}-u_{ik}+u_{jk}=0\qquad(i<j<k).
$$
Indeed differentiating a remaining even box inserts a third $B$ with the sign from the preceding odd factors. Thus $u_{ij}=v_j-v_i$ for vertex potentials constant on every nonconsecutive pair. For $r\ge4$ the graph of nonconsecutive pairs is connected. Consequently $y=0$.

A surface witness in this case supplies a rational nonnegative rank-$d$ chain whose differential differs from the required one by just such a cycle, so the difference vanishes. The chain differs from the integral particular solution by a rational top boundary. To get an integral positive filler, index its correcting potential by the tuple of box choices. Each rank-$d$ coefficient has the form $z_{0,e}+w_{\rm prod}-w_{\rm cons}$: the sign at each dropped box is positive because all preceding boxes are even, and the phase edge has at most one producing and one consuming box. Use potential zero at missing endpoints. Rounding all potentials down preserves these integer difference inequalities. This gives the required independent integral adjustment on $C$. For $r\ge4$ this proves reflection in the last unclassified rank; for $r=3$ that rank has global degree six.

**The three-slot test.** With three slots the nonconsecutive-pair graph has the two components $\{1,3\}$ and $\{2\}$. The preceding cocycle calculation describes the extra freedom exactly. For each box tuple the change in a signed rank-five chain with quotient-zero differential is a sum of single-$B_i$ words, with one potential shared by axes one and three, and an independent potential on axis two. To see necessity, the vertex component of its differential forces the separate phase sums to vanish. In the single-$B_i$ bases the coefficient on a pair $B_i,B_j$ in the differential is the difference of the two potentials. It must vanish on nonconsecutive pairs, and those are all the restrictions. Thus the model's nonnegativity test splits the original grid of difference inequalities into these two groups. Each group again permits integer potentials by rounding.

For each prescribed triple of update counts the checker quantifies over **actual parallel strict 4-faces**: both nonnegative integral top rows have the same differential, each common lower pair satisfies its tableau boundary equations and both vertex rows augment to one. It asks for an integral particular $5$-chain at this boundary with feasible split inequalities and infeasible original inequalities. The latter is a negative path from the exterior back to itself in the grid of box tuples; the internal grid is acyclic. Unsatisfiability proves reflection at every such input pair. Z3 returns unsatisfiable for all eight triples with one or two updates independently per slot. On the single-update triple the rational relaxation instead returns satisfiable, so integrality of the old faces matters. The earlier clique gluing then gives the stated interval result even when several maximum triples occur. This leaves the unrestricted update multiplicities in the degree-six exception open. [Square quotient and endomorphism condition](#researcher-response-109) · [Lower degree witnesses](#researcher-response-92)

## Researcher Response 111

**The exact failing degrees above three in every weighted globular Gray interval are $4,\ldots,M+1$, with no exception.** Here $M$ is the maximum reversed-subsequence weight after forcing two consecutive members to be intervals, with at least three members, as in Response 92. With no such subsequence there is no failure above three. This holds for each binary surface containing interchange, any private update multiplicities and any spatial width. In particular on three fully reversed and fully updated strands the only failing degrees above three are four and five, regardless of how many successive changes each strand carries. We resolve the degree-six case of Response 110 by recovering a full integral tensor filler from a path of phase changes.

Keep the three fully updated slots of a maximum clique. In the tensor complex each slot has two vertices, parallel phase edges in sequence and a box between each successive pair of phases. Take parallel old local 4-faces $s,t$ in this tensor. Keep from each top chain only cells active in **all three** slots. Three phase edges specify a vertex of a new grid, one phase coordinate per strand. A local 4-atom with one box and two phase edges specifies a unit edge in this grid. Orient the first and third coordinates by increasing phase and the middle by decreasing phase. The all-active part of the tensor differential of that 4-atom is exactly the target minus the source in these orientations: the sign at its box is $(-1)^{i-1}$ in spatial slot $i$. A local 5-atom has two boxes and a single phase edge. Its all-active differential is the boundary of the unit grid square on those two box coordinates, in spatial order, with the ordinary directed orientation from right-first to left-first. For the earlier box the tensor sign combined with its coordinate reversal is positive, and for the later box it is negative because there is one additional preceding box instead of an edge. Thus no pair of grid directions requires the opposite convention.

**The two faces give actual paths.** In either local 3-boundary row of $s,t$ there is at most one all-active triple of phase edges, with coefficient one. Indeed collapse all the updates to identities and their phases to the edges of the bare three-cube. The number of top triple atoms in the resulting 3-row is the original all-active count. In the bare cube a 2-reading between temporal paths exchanges a particular pair at most once. Thus each of its square coordinates is zero or one. The difference of two such 2-rows is the triple count times the signed boundary of the bare cube, with a unit coefficient in each facet. This bounds the nonnegative triple count by one. If a 3-face lies on a smaller part of the cube the same bound applies. Projecting the two local 4-faces to all-active terms now gives integral, nonnegative edge flows on the oriented phase grid. Each has the common lower 3-rows as its two projected ends. The grid is acyclic, so a flow with no net boundary is zero, and a unit flow from one vertex to another is a single monotone path. Denote the resulting two phase paths by $u,v$, using empty paths when there is no movement.

For any pair of axes $j<k$, project the phase paths onto them. There is a unique signed 2-chain on this planar rectangular grid with boundary $v|_{jk}-u|_{jk}$, by contractibility and top injectivity. Write its coefficients as $T_{jk}(p,q)$, indexed by the individual updates in those directions. They are $+1$ for a change from right-first to left-first, $-1$ for a change in the opposite direction, and zero for unchanged relative order. This follows either by the unit squares between the two paths in the rectangle, or by sorting the two-colour shuffles and taking signed swaps. Fixed occurrences in the decreasing middle coordinate are indexed in their order of execution.

These integers are forced at the original boundary even after surface conversion. Take an integral particular 5-chain $z_0$ as in Response 110. Summing its coefficients on the squares for $p,q$ over all phase positions of the third axis gives exactly $T_{jk}(p,q)$, by projection of the all-active differential onto the rectangle. In the **full** tensor differential the coefficient at boxes $p,q$ and the *upper vertex* of that third slot is this very sum: only dropping its phase edge can produce the vertex, with positive sign since preceding boxes have even degree. The lower vertex has the negative of this coefficient. These vertex-and-two-box basis elements survive freely in the degree-four square quotient. ## Researcher Response 113

**Q1 in each degree reduces to contexts with one object and exactly two generating arrows, for both kernels and all the surfaces in the question.** Higher declarations retain their ranks and may have arbitrary attaching terms. More precisely, there is an effective translation of any nonempty finite context and any particular old type of degree at least two to such a context and a type of the *same degree*. Inhabitation is preserved and reflected separately in the raw theory and in each surface theory, including published strict units and insertion. Two arrows are optimal for a substitution that reflects all individual old judgments in this way.

### Encoding the generating arrows

Use the object identification of [Response 20](#researcher-response-20), which reflects each of the stated judgments in degree at least two. Call the resulting one-object context $G$, and enumerate its generating arrows $f_1,\ldots,f_m$. The new context $E$ has one object and two loops $P,Q$. Translate $f_i$ to the right-associated path with spelling
$$
                         c_i=P(PQ)^iQ .
$$
For every generator of degree at least two, adjoin one fresh generator at its literally translated type. This defines a raw substitution $e$ on all of $G$. It preserves inhabitation by substitution in each theory. The difficulty with a converse is that a term in $E$ can insert a rule with empty input *inside* a codeword. Decoding only paths with a fixed partition into codewords would miss such terms.

Let $K$ be the set of finite nonempty stacks of natural numbers, with a permanent bottom frame. Each letter acts on any starting stack and outputs either an old arrow or the raw identity. $P$ pushes a zero and outputs the identity. $Q$ at the bottom alone fixes the stack and outputs the identity. Otherwise it pops the top frame. A popped zero increments the new top and outputs the identity. A popped positive integer $j$ leaves the rest of the stack untouched and outputs $f_j$ if $j\le m$, and the identity otherwise. During $c_i$ the initial push creates a private frame. Each inner $PQ$ increments just that frame. The final pop outputs $f_i$ and restores the *entire* starting stack. Thus from every state $c_i$ has identity state action and the very same raw readout $k_i(f_i)$, the prescribed right-associated composite of $|c_i|-1$ identities followed by $f_i$. In particular an empty word and every encoded word have identical state actions. The stack set is used only in a model of the finite presentation.

### Interpreting a term at an arbitrary stack

Here are the model details needed to decode even a filler obtained by conversion. For a one-object model $M$ of the theory in use, form a one-object model $W(M)$. An arrow consists of a function $h:K\to K$ and a family of arrows of $M$ indexed by $K$. In degree $r\ge2$ a cell consists of a function $h$ and a family of $r$-cells of $M$. Its positive-dimensional faces have the same function and the corresponding pointwise faces. The cells of identity state action form the submodel $M^K$.

To interpret a head, label its globular arity in $W(M)$. In each spatial column all arrow positions have one common state function, since the child tree connects these positions by 2-faces. For a chosen initial state $a$, compute the state at each successive spine vertex by these column functions. Evaluate each positive-dimensional label in $M$ at its column's initial state. Object labels go to the single object. This gives an actual labelling in $M$, since taking any positive-dimensional face inside a column keeps its initial state. Apply the given head of $M$ to that tuple. Use the terminal-state function of the whole spine as the state action of the result. A head on the point keeps its starting state.

For verification, an expression supported between spine vertices $i$ and $j$ acts there by the consecutive column functions and has the value obtained by evaluating the expression on those indexed labels. At a variable this is the labelling rule. At a substituted head the spine of each argument covers its corresponding interval; concatenation computes the same successive states, including on intervals of length zero. This proves the assertion by induction, hence also the face and substitution rules. The same argument starts at *any* state at vertex $i$ when only that subinterval is used. No inverse of a state function is needed. For a generic binary equation, the two words have the same outer poles and use the same column states on that interval; the equation and the prescribed coherence equation then hold in $M$ at every initial state. For disc and endo-coherence removal use respectively the disc label and the common face at that state. In pruning a pruned identity acts trivially on states where it is an arrow; inside a column its two positive faces have the same function. In insertion the interior labelling subdivides the same spine interval or lies inside one column, so the joined tuple on both sides is the same indexed tuple. The corresponding equations of $M$ apply. This checks $W(M)$ in both kernels using their actual heads and in all the specified quotients. In particular the construction does not require a surface model structure.

### Returning to the literal old boundary

Write $H$ for the free raw model on $G$. There is a raw endomorphism $d:H\to H$, homotopic to the identity, with $d(f_i)=k_i(f_i)$. To see this first work on the free raw arrow disc. The two labels of its top arrow, the generic arrow and its padded expression (identities at its source), agree on their exact endpoints and have the same strict value. The raw disc maps by a trivial fibration to its strict image in either kernel. Lift a relative cylinder of the disc against this map over the common strict label. This gives a homotopy between the two assignments fixing the boundary. Substitute the loop $f_i$ and glue these relative paths at the vertex, obtaining a path on the whole generating graph from the inclusion to the padded labelling. In the mapping-space notation of [Response 24](#researcher-response-24), restriction $M(H,H)\to M(H_{G_{\le1}},H)$ is a Kan fibration because the graph inclusion is cellular and $H$ is fibrant. Lift the graph path starting at $1_H$. Its endpoint is the required $d$. This step handles all higher declarations at once, including those attached at composites involving old coherences. [Raw globe and fibrancy inputs](#researcher-response-3)

Now take $Y$ to be the free model of the chosen theory on $G$, and $q:H\to Y$ its raw interpretation. Interpret $E$ in $W(Y)$. Assign its loops the two stack operations with their indicated outputs in $Y$. Assign every higher generator corresponding to $z$ the constant family $qd(z)$ with identity state action. These assignments have their declared types: on each encoded arrow the family is exactly the constant $qk_i(f_i)$, and the typing assertion in higher ranks follows in declaration order by substitution into the translated attaching terms. Thus on the entire old raw model the composite with $e$ is the diagonal of $qd$.

Let $b:B_r\to H$ be the specified old boundary, $r\ge2$. A filler at $eb$ gives in $W(Y)$ a cell at the diagonal of $qdb$. Its arrow faces have identity state action, so it belongs to $Y^K$. Its endpoint fills exactly $qb$, proving reflection. For a one-object starting context the assertion in degrees zero and one is immediate as well. For the universal question these degrees always reflect by the edge-path argument of Response 20. The construction therefore preserves the least dimension of a failure when one exists.

There are two stronger conclusions for the encoding of a one-object $G$. If the surface includes $U$, every $k_i(f_i)$ equals $f_i$ definitionally: the rank-one left unit law is a parallel word law on the arrow disc. The same exact return works for strict images of either kernel. For an ordinary strict one-object target, the family operations compose pointwise with reindexing by the first arrow's state function. For a Gray-enriched strict target with hom $L$, the new hom is the coproduct over functions $h$ of $L^K$. On a pair of components $h,k$, its Gray tensor composition has component $k\circ h$ and coordinate $a$ given by the two projections at $a,h(a)$ tensored together followed by the original enriched composition. These specify the composition on the coproduct since the Gray tensor preserves coproducts separately. Both triple composites use the projections at $a,h(a),k(h(a))$, so enriched associativity and the unit follow from those of the target. Now interpret in the respective free strict image of $G$: each code evaluates to its original generator at every stack. Giving every higher declaration its original diagonal value therefore reflects strict equality, and also reflects existence of strict cells at old boundaries of degree at least two. In particular the return retains the directed tensor cells present in the Gray strict image.

For sharpness take the free graph on one vertex and two loops $a,b$. The old type $ab\to ba$ has no raw filler by ordinary strict projection. Under any substitution into a one-object context with just one generating arrow, the two image paths have the same strict arrow, a power of the unique generator. Every raw arrow term uses only the graph: an arrow head is on a linear path or the point. Unroll both substituted composites on the linear path of that total length, retaining their actual brackets and identities. Their strict images are the same full path, so a generic raw coherence between these writings exists in either kernel. For length zero use the point. This description is integral: a relation is an exterior tensor of either a killed square or its boundary; if another edge is active in its block both sides already vanish. Edge counts, counts on a specified phase edge, and vertex augmentations therefore descend. In particular a nonnegative term surviving this block test cannot disappear by a positive relation.

A derivative in any other column has zero evaluation, since both polar faces there contribute equally. ### Exactly when several source and target terms can share the intermediate cell

Fix finite nonempty sets $U,V$ of raw $(r-1)$-terms, all of one literal type $A$, in a finite computad $G$. Select any family of its named $r$-generators with sources in $U$ and targets in $V$. This specifies the raw map $e:G\to E$ in the direction of free models. Higher attaching terms may use any of the selected generators. Then the following are equivalent.

1. Every pair in $U\times V$ has a raw $r$-cell $u\to v$ in $G$.
2. Translation reflects inhabitation of every old raw type in the raw kernel and, separately, in every surface above it listed in the question.

### Which attachments can alter an old type in either kernel?

For a computad inclusion $A\subseteq X$ in either kernel, an old degree-$k$ type, $k\ge1$, has **exactly the same raw fillers and the same surface filler classes** under weakening if no new degree-$k$ generator is present. There may be new generators in every other rank. More precisely, even in the presence of new $k$-generators there is a polynomial-time test on their incidence counts that confines *all* old degree-$k$ judgments simultaneously to a subcomputad.

Its closed support is contained in the closed support of its $(k-1)$-source and the attaching closures of the generating $k$-cells used, including those cells themselves. Indeed one can serialize any strict $k$-paste as successive single $k$-generators in stationary contexts: at a lower binary cut, execute the left sequence with the right source fixed, then the right sequence with the left target fixed, by strict interchange. At a top cut concatenate. Stationary factors of an elementary step already occur in its source; the only additional support can come from the generating step. This proves the claim by induction, including the identity paste. Response 27 identifies cells over a subcomputad with the pullback along its ordinary strict inclusion for each kernel and surface. Thus the support assertion also covers surface classes at the exact old faces. In particular a degree-$k$ failure in $A$ persists in any extension having no new generators of that degree.

For the incidence test take one Petri place for every new $(k-1)$-generator, and one transition per new $k$-generator. The two vectors of that transition count the places in its ordinary strict source and target, with multiplicity. At $k=1$ count the endpoint vertex. In the serialization above, stationary factors supply exactly the additional tokens; for a path of edges the token is simply its current vertex restricted to the new places. Old steps project to no change and have no new ports. Hence the list of new top steps in any filler at an old boundary is a firing sequence from zero back to zero. Keep $A$ and the attaching closures of the transitions occurring on at least one such sequence. The support argument gives a bijection on every one of the indicated filler sets after this restriction. Drewes and Leroux compute the set of transitions on zero returns in polynomial time in the supplied net; parallel labels with identical profiles may all be retained when that profile is retained. [Drewes–Leroux, Theorem 6.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.08331#page=8) · [Support pullback for both kernels](#researcher-response-27)

There is a sharpness statement for the port data alone. For each fixed $k\ge3$, any net with a zero return using a designated transition has an ordinary realization in which that transition helps supply a genuinely new old degree-$k$ inhabitant. Put $m=k-1$. Take one old $m$-scalar $g$ at a point and adjoin one $m$-scalar per place. Give each net transition a $k$-generator with its stated input and output multisets written as top composites, and add one copy of $g$ to the output of the designated transition. An empty multiset is the identity. A firing sequence has a raw realization: bracket the available inputs together, apply the declaration with stationary factors and reassemble its output. Any two orderings and bracketings of the same multiset admit raw comparisons at the standard scalar boundary, since ordered $m$-dimensional configurations are connected for $m\ge2$. Empty products and identity paddings use the raw unit comparisons. [Scalar configurations at fixed boundaries](#researcher-response-38) A zero return with $l>0$ occurrences of the designated transition therefore supplies a raw cell from the empty scalar composite to $g^l$. On the old base the two strict values are distinct and only identity $k$-cells exist. Every ordinary surface distinguishes that old judgment there. In particular, if *every* transition emits one old $g$, unchanged inhabitation at all old degree-$k$ types of these explicit scalar extensions is equivalent to absence of a nonempty zero return. For explicit port lists this special preservation problem is P-complete, by closure of P under complement and the unary hardness in Drewes–Leroux, Corollary 6.4. This classifies preservation under extension; the surface-versus-raw classification on arbitrary $D$ still requires the tests on the retained presentation.

**Joining several temporal events in a single target column.** In the nonrepeatable case spatial join is a strict partial order on the occupied pole pairs: each slot has a nonempty edge path between its own poles. Assign integer levels $1,\ldots,m$ to slots so that each joining pair has strictly increasing levels. Let $H(v)$ be the maximum level of a slot whose target can reach the object $v$, including zero in the maximum. Along an edge $H$ is nondecreasing. At a slot of level $j$ from $x$ to $y$ one has $H(x)<j\le H(y)$. In a named ordinary diagram send every vertex over $v$ to $H(v)$, and let every wire over $x\to y$ carry exactly the levels in $(H(x),H(y)]$, in order. Every temporal frontier thus carries the same interval of levels once each. A box acts only on the token of its own level. Two simultaneously enabled boxes have disjoint level intervals containing their respective tokens, so their levels are distinct and in physical spatial order. All occurrences acting on a given token are totally ordered by wire dependence: if incomparable, the union of their predecessor ideals would enable both.

For each token take the target column to be the ordered temporal path with the private tree of each of its successive events. On every wire use the vertex of this path given by the number of these events already executed. The vertex stays constant while the wire is live since any change consumes the wire carrying that token. At a box, the other tokens traversing its input and output paths retain their vertices, while its own token advances one event. ## Researcher Response 129

**There is a dichotomy for the degreewise Q1 and Q2 questions.** Fix either kernel, one of its surfaces, and a degree $k\ge3$. If there is *any* finite context where conservativity in degree $k$ fails, there is an effective family of finite one-object contexts with the following properties.

* Their entire $(k-1)$-skeleton is fixed. Every raw type in positive degree below $k$ is inhabited.
* On acceptance of the input by a fixed universal machine, **every raw $k$-type** is inhabited. On nonacceptance, one fixed old $k$-type witnesses failure of conservativity.
* Consequently degree-$k$ conservativity of the **whole context** on this family is r.e.-complete. An algorithm deciding the individual-context question in degree $k$ on all finite inputs exists exactly when the degree-$k$ universal assertion in Q1 is true.

For the four Gray surfaces containing $I$ this is unconditional in every $k\ge3$, simultaneously on the same family. Its **exact spectrum of failing degrees** is $\{k+1,k+2,\ldots\}$ on acceptance and $\{k,k+1,\ldots\}$ on nonacceptance. Thus even distinguishing two adjacent candidates for the first failing degree is undecidable under the promise that these are the only possibilities. In contrast to a computation at one prescribed boundary, acceptance here supplies raw inhabitants at *every* boundary of the tested degree.

### A finite list of raw repairs

First let $D$ be a finite one-object computad, and fix a rank cap $d$. In either kernel one can effectively include $D_{\le d}$ in a finite $d$-computad $C_{\le d}$ over the same vertex in which every raw type through degree $d$ is inhabited. The notation comes from the following infinite presentation, finite in each degree. Begin with the point. At each old positive-dimensional declaration $z:A$ of rank $j$, the presentation constructed so far is weakly equivalent to the point. Hence at its actual already included attaching terms there is a raw $j$-cell $u:A$: take the iterated hom at the prescribed faces in the realization, or lift the globe boundary against the map to the point. Attach a fresh parallel copy of $u$ by the $j$-fold suspension of the coherent walking equivalence $E$ of Response 13. More precisely push out the inclusion $D_j\to\Sigma^j E$ of the first suspended vertex along the raw globe map for $u$. Name the second suspended vertex $z$. It has precisely the declared type $A$, including its original syntax.

In the ordinary realization that inclusion is an equivalence because suspension preserves the endpoint equivalence $*\to E$. For the Gray realization $j\ge1$: take the first $j-1$ suspensions in the ordinary theory and use one outer directed enriched suspension. The only forward hom is the ordinary suspended presentation, the stationary homs are points and the reverse hom is empty. Thus the inclusion is again an equivalence. Globe attachments compute homotopy pushouts in these realizations, including a sequence of attachments along the free globe inclusion at a composite $u$. The enlarged presentation remains weakly equivalent to the point. These are the weak walking equivalence and cellular realization inputs of [Response 13](#researcher-response-13) and [the fixed-hom realization theorem](../answered/catt-models-unit-condition-r4-2026-11-20.md#researcher-response-16). [Fujii–Hoshino–Maehara, §5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09849) · [Benjamin–Champin–Markakis, computadic expansion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30254)

Each step contributes one new $j$-name and $3\cdot2^{a-1}$ names of degree $j+a$ for $a\ge1$ in the separate-inverse presentation of $E$. To find $u$, enumerate raw terms and their typing derivations in the finite $j$-skeleton of the preceding stages. Existence just proved makes the search terminate. The finite stages needed in the end can thus be computed without an oracle. A raw filler of degree at most $d$ in the infinite union uses only its $d$-skeleton, by the arity bound. This establishes the assertion even for types involving the auxiliary generators.

Two consequences apply to both kernels. First, any old degree-$k$ failure can be made a *first* failure in the same degree. Fold the objects by [Response 20](#researcher-response-20), apply the construction through $k-1$, and retain the original degree-$k$ declarations at their old types. The inclusion adds no degree-$k$ generator, so [Response 124](#researcher-response-124) preserves every raw filler and surface filler class at every old $k$-boundary. This also preserves all the fixed and varying old judgments of [Response 123](#researcher-response-123) after folding. Second, raw inhabitation of **all** types through $d$ on finite one-object inputs is r.e.: a certificate is a raw map $C_{\le d}\to D_{\le d}$ fixing the input, specified by a finite tuple of well-typed terms. Such a map suffices by substitution and exists under the assertion by lifting the additional declarations in order. In particular, given a fixed raw-complete lower skeleton, one can prepare a finite test list for the next degree. Take a return on the lower skeleton of its completion, and apply it to the attaching types of the finitely many next-degree declarations. If these have fillers, the return extends across that cap. This last test works for existence of surface fillers at all *old* boundaries too, using the raw lower return and evaluating the raw completed presentation in the surface reduct.

### A common lower skeleton for all inputs

Let $B$ be a finite counterexample in degree $k$, folded to one object and restricted to its $k$-skeleton. Write $m=k-2$. If $1_b\to P_b$ has a raw filler, this gives a raw filler for the original $s\to t$. Use a fixed deterministic universal tape machine with a finite positive substring presentation. On input $w$ its initial word is $W=L_0q_0wR_0$ and its cleaned accepting word is $A=L_0q_aR_0$. The delimiters $L_0,R_0$ are preserved until exit. Each instruction contains a state; it can mention $L_0$ only as a leftmost symbol and $R_0$ only as a rightmost symbol.  \begin{array}{lll}
 1_h\to W,& \ell\to r\quad\text{for each instruction},& A\to P_h,\\
 1_b\to[W]_b,& & [A]_b\to P_b\qquad(b\in V\text{ of type }T).

There are no declarations above rank $k$. Only the input words of the initializations vary.

If the machine accepts, its successive substring moves yield a raw $k$-cell $W\to A$. Carry a rule at the prefix and suffix by temporal whiskering, using the raw comparisons for the chosen bracketings on the temporal string. This works in the directed kernel since these cuts are within a single hom. Initialization and exit, with $o_b,c_b$ on the two sides in the second row, give all $1_b\to P_b$ and $1_h\to P_h$. The raw interpretation $C'_{\le k}\to X_w$ of the completed presentation in the constructed context is therefore the identity on $L$ and fits every repair. Every raw $k$-type over $X_w$ has its boundary on $L$ and so receives a raw filler by this interpretation. Below $k$ the raw conclusion already holds on $L$.

### Excluding a raw repair when the machine does not accept

We use a weak ordinary target that remembers which letters lie on a common wire. Construct a strict symmetric monoidal 2-category as follows. Objects are finite numbers of ports. A 1-arrow is a finite directed wire diagram, up to isomorphism fixing its ordered exterior ports. Wires start at input ports or fresh openings and finish at output ports or fresh closings. Each carries a word in the tape alphabet in order along it. Also allow isolated marks $P$. Equivalently take the free symmetric monoidal category on one object $H$, an opening $I\to H$, a closing $H\to I$, letter endomorphisms of $H$, and $P:I\to I$. Composition glues the matching ports, concatenating words on the resulting wires. Tensor is ordered disjoint union with the usual permutation symmetries. Closed components and isolated marks remain components under whiskering.

For parallel diagrams $a,b$, a 2-arrow is a number $j\ge0$ such that $j$ elementary steps in contexts take $a$ to $b$. The steps are the following.

* Insert $W$ at any position on a wire, apply a tape instruction to a substring on a wire, or replace the substring $A$ by the empty word and an isolated $P$.
* Add a separate closed wire bearing $W$, or replace a whole closed wire bearing $A$ by an isolated $P$.
* From any diagram with an isolated $P$, go to any parallel diagram.

Here the contexts are tensor and composition with stationary diagrams on either side. A step on a wire remains the indicated substring step after gluing. The two closed-component steps remain closed-component steps. In the last case the composite source still has an isolated $P$. Vertical composition, horizontal composition and tensor add lengths; when two moves act in parallel, perform them in separate factors. Thus counts define actual 2-arrows at the composite boundaries, and strict interchange follows from addition. The symmetry is natural also on 2-arrows, since it preserves the count. An invertible 2-arrow necessarily has length zero. Keeping the count distinguishes a computation from an identity at the same boundary.

In this 2-category there is **no positive-length 2-arrow from the empty diagram back to itself on a nonaccepting input**. Before the first exit or use of a mark, each state is a multiset of closed wires, each labelled by a word obtained from copies of the initial delimited word and the instructions. Subsequent insertions can nest inside a previous session or lie beside it. Delimiters stay properly matched. For any matched pair, omit the complete words inside its immediately nested pairs. What remains between its delimiters is a configuration reachable from the original input. At insertion the new pair starts there and the other projections stay fixed. An instruction has no internal delimiter and cannot consume a right delimiter on its left or a left delimiter on its right. Its nondelimiter letters and state therefore belong to one level of this matching. If it uses an end delimiter it uses the corresponding end of that session. Its projection there is a legal instruction and all other projections remain unchanged. Any occurrence of $A$ would consequently certify acceptance. Until then the steps can neither erase a closed wire nor produce a mark. From the empty diagram the first positive step must add a closed wire. Ordered incidence is essential here: two isomorphic presentations of several wires may rename intermediate ports together, but cannot reconnect only one end of those wires.

To interpret the rank-$k$ count, take the $m$-fold delooping of this symmetric monoidal higher category, restricting its symmetric monoidal action to $E_m$. Its fixed $m$-fold hom is the displayed 2-category. This is the pointed enriched-category construction used in [Response 36](#researcher-response-36), also for noninvertible arrows. The symmetric monoidal 2-functor recording lengths lands in the 2-category with one object, one 1-arrow and additive $\mathbb N$ as 2-arrows. Its $m$-fold delooping is the ordinary strict rank-$k$ counter: a singleton below $k$, additive $k$-cells and identities above. Equivalently take the iterated single-object enrichment, with strictly commutative addition in this target. [Gepner–Haugseng, §6.3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3178)

Here are the generator assignments, with the weak-boundary details. Send the pre-tape presentation $C_{\le k-1}$ and the original $B$ to the distinguished point, so its $m$-cells give the tensor unit $I$. Send each $h_T$ to $H$. Assign openings, closings and letters as in the wire category, $P_b$ to the isolated mark at $I$, and $P_h$ to the identity wire with an isolated mark. Other $(m+1)$-arrows of the walking attachment at $b_0$ can use openings or closings in their declared directions. In particular these assignments cover the entire lower presentation. Temporal composites on one $h$ read words in order; $[u]_b$ gives a separate closed wire with word $u$. Each program declaration has its one step, and each conditional repair has a one-step interpretation because its source contains an isolated mark. Each original $k$-declaration has count zero. These choices define the map on the cellular ordinary realization. More explicitly, choose the indicated representatives in the fixed hom. At each globe attachment, transport along the boundary identifications by the globe restriction fibration. The tensor-unit identifications and the composition constraints are invertible; changing a representative of a wire diagram by a boundary identification transports the chosen arrow with it. At the top this leaves its count fixed. In particular the composite with the strict counter is the map determined by the stated numbers on the declared $k$-generators: any endpoint transports there are identities. For the Gray syntax first use the ordinary interpretation of its heads over their full ordinary projections from [Response 1](#researcher-response-1), translating the attaching terms by the same substitution rule. The program uses only the temporal operations. Their generic translations have the indicated ordinary strict values and are equivalent to the chosen temporal pastes on their globular arities. Alternatively evaluate those operations by the arity lifting choices using the ordinary temporal operations themselves. The ordinary interpretation is used only to bound the top occurrence count; the original obstruction remains in its own kernel.

In particular the image of a raw filler of the chosen old type would be an endomorphism of the empty diagram, with length equal to the total occurrences of the **new** $k$-declarations in its ordinary strict paste. Old $B$-cells have constant image. On nonacceptance this length must be zero. The support argument of Response 124 puts that paste in $B$: start from its old source and serialize its steps, all of which would be old. The support pullback of Response 27 then puts the raw filler itself at the old boundary in $B$, contrary to the choice of the type. Its surface filler weakens from $B$ for every input. This proves the dichotomy. In the nonuniversal case, failure in degree $k$ on all finite contexts cannot even be recognized by enumerating finite certificates: on this family that would recognize nonacceptance. It also proves r.e.-completeness on this family of the separate property that every raw type is inhabited through $k$. For that last assertion alone any old raw-negative $k$-type suffices, for instance two distinct parallel $(k-1)$-generators without a $k$-rule.

Finally, in Gray degree three use one point, a loop edge and a 2-endomorphism of that edge, with the old reverse of its exchange at two spatial positions. For higher $k$ take the one-scalar context with the folded cube boundary of Response 29. These supply a common old failure for all four choices of surface. ## Researcher Response 130

**An integral gluing test resolves every open degree of the mixed planar example in Response 128.** Its exact failing global degrees are three, four and five. More generally one may split the spatial join graph at a shared set of slots and solve the two sides separately. Above the maximum joined weight of the shared set, the two positive fillers glue at the original old boundary, even when their event orderings interleave in time. The test can be iterated. In the example, put the tall slot on one side, the three elementary slots which it spans on the other, and the first elementary slot in the shared set. Its weight is one. The two projections have the bounds of a two-column string and a four-interval string, respectively, giving the asserted result at every private height of the spanning slot.

**The chain gluing lemma.** Use the named comparison of Response 127 and the order $R$ common to the two temporal readings of given parallel old faces in global degree at least four. Retain each event's private tree between two distinct poles. The decorated ideal complex $X(R)$ has one basis word for each admissible cut with its active antichain and chosen positive-rank basis cell in each active coordinate. The other coordinates are at their two poles. Restricting to a set $Y$ of events gives a chain projection onto $X(R|Y)$: an active omitted factor contributes zero, and a stationary omitted factor contributes its augmentation one. The tensor sign and differential commute with these maps. The actual old faces are tableaux in this complex in the order of the all-event projection. A positive chain with their prescribed differential gives a filler by that same tensor test and its return at the old boundary. [Named planar judgment](#researcher-response-127) · [Decorated interval tableaux](#researcher-response-110)

Partition the events into exclusive sets $A,B$ and a shared set $S$, with every member of $A$ comparable to every member of $B$ in $R$. Take the projections which retain $A\cup S$ and $B\cup S$. A basis atom in the first projection with an active member $a\in A$ has exactly one lift: every $b\in B$ preceding $a$ must already be complete, and every one following $a$ must still be pending. This gives consistent choices even when several $A$-members are active, since they are an antichain. The cut is valid by transitivity. For instance a completed retained coordinate with a pending predecessor $b$ would have the active $a$ as a predecessor as well. The other cut conditions follow by the same comparisons, including those on newly completed members of $B$. The statement is symmetric for a $B$-exclusive atom.

The **pair of projections is jointly injective on integral chains in every rank**, including ranks with entirely shared active support. The exclusive coefficients are read individually by the preceding observation. For the others fix all shared coordinates, including their polar vertices and private basis labels. A possible stationary cut on $A\cup B$ is an edge of a bipartite graph whose endpoints are its separate restrictions to $A$ and $B$. Its two integral marginals are exactly the corresponding projected coefficients. This bipartite graph is a forest. To see this, choose a linear extension on $A\cup B$ and split it into maximal monochrome runs. All members of an earlier run precede every member of the next run in the order itself, by cross-comparability. Thus in any ideal only one run can be partly executed. Its possible subideals give a star in the bipartite graph, centered at the fixed cut of the other colour. Successive stars share just the edge at their common seam; a new non-seam partial cut on the changing side occurs in no previous star. Their union is a tree (or a single edge for empty input). The conditions from the fixed $S$-coordinates only restrict this edge set. On a finite forest a signed edge weighting with both vertex marginals zero vanishes by pruning leaves. This proves the injectivity without any positivity assumption.

Suppose the queried local rank $k$ exceeds the maximum rank of an entirely $S$-active atom. Every rank-$k$ atom in either piece then has an exclusive coordinate. Take any nonnegative integral filler on each side and lift its exclusive coefficients to the unique corresponding full words. These two disjoint sets of coefficients give one nonnegative integral $k$-chain. Its two projections are the proposed fillers. Its boundary projects to the two required differences, so the joint injectivity one rank lower identifies it with the full prescribed difference. Hence it gives the required strict, and then raw, filler. The strict inequality on rank is needed in this argument only for the top chain. The common boundary may use the shared set in its full dimension.

**Applying the lemma to a finite base.** Use the undirected graph whose vertices are occupied pole pairs and whose edges join two spatially composable slots in either order. Cross occurrences have the same relative temporal order in both old readings: otherwise they would be incomparable in the wire-dependence order, hence co-enabled and spatially composable. The gluing hypothesis follows. An antichain of active shared occurrences is a spatially joined string, so its total local rank is at most the maximum joined weight $W(S)$ in the shared graph. Nonrepeatability ensures that no type occurs twice in this string.

All smaller projections used in a recursive proof can be made directly from the original unfolded surface witness. For a leaf keep just its marked occurrences, assigning every other box the identity on its entire carried word. In the construction of Response 128 compute levels using the retained *slot types*, and use throughout the original edge reachability, including paths through the other types' poles. Both sides of an omitted box still carry the same concatenation of tokens at the same phases. If the leaf bound reflects, it gives a raw filler in the grouped chart. Expand its event names and restrict its intermediate words to the common temporal order on this subset as in Response 127. On incomparable co-enabled events its orientation agrees with the all-event axis order. Thus it gives the required positive filler in the leaf complex; the construction requires no realization of the restricted temporal diagram as an independent presented input. ## Researcher Response 131

**The interchange failure spectrum is exact for every finite positive planar Gray 2-base with private globular generators in arbitrary higher dimensions.** No uniform-height, spatial-width or bound on temporal repetitions is needed.
