## Researcher Response 200

**With private 3-rules in just the left column, arbitrary positive long 3-rules are allowed.** Positivity here concerns only the *entire* temporal input and output. Either projection of either face can be empty; a long rule can, for instance, consume only left wires and produce only right wires. Keep the two-column 2-skeleton and unrestricted positive private left rules of Response 198, with no private right rule or higher declaration. For every binary Gray surface all old judgments above degree three reflect. Degree four admits the polynomial-time algorithm below and from degree five onwards every parallel old boundary has a raw filler. Consequently all-dimensional conservativity for a surface containing interchange is exactly the finite elementary-return condition and is r.e.-complete here. This covers cyclic transfers between columns, which need not give a positive planar occurrence complex in either projection.

### The mixed incidence and its two wire words

In a 3-reading carry input wire names through native swaps and give each non-swap vertex its rule name and ordered input wire origins. Name its output wires by that vertex and output port. Total positivity identifies all these occurrences even if the left projection of a shared input is empty. Retain the joint port incidence and the final output wires. For each left wire e record the right wire names W(e) crossing it in chronological order. For each right wire f record the chronological word V(f) of left wires crossing it. Each pair crosses at most once: a native swap reverses that pair's relative order, and other vertices preserve the order of live wires they do not consume.

First require identical joint incidence at the two faces. Perform the prefix divisions of [Response 198](#researcher-response-198) on the W-words in joint causal order, with an empty move word at every nonprivate occurrence. Only private left polygons require a word to be inferred, and each has an input. As each forced private move of p past f is replayed, replace the input list of p by its output list inside V(f). At the end require literal equality of the V-words too. This second record supplies order information even when there is no left planar path complex from which to read it.

The replay is valid without a hypothesis on either projected arity of a shared rule. At a forced move f is the *last* crossing on every input wire of p. These inputs feed p directly after their swaps. The swaps along f occur in the input order of p: each crossed wire remains inert to its left, and each subsequent crossed input is placed to its right. There cannot be another swap between consecutive ones. After any intervening crossing, there is a nonempty temporal subword between the earlier inert wire and f. While f lives it can only draw another wire into this subword; the inert wire is untouched. Every other rewrite within it preserves nonemptiness by total positivity. After the next input crossing a nonempty subword would therefore remain between the two inert inputs until p, contradicting their adjacency at p. Thus the full input path is consecutive on f. The last-swap contraction of Response 194 exposes the native negative prism face. Its replacement gives precisely the update of V(f) used by the algorithm. The final two families of wire words and the non-swap incidence reconstruct every vertex and every ordered wire of the mixed diagram, hence suffice for raw equality.

### Why surface conversion cannot permute the final word on a right wire

Use a strict long-hom model indexed by the joint coloured port incidence. Its W-data and positive private move words are those of Response 198 in the free group of right wire occurrences. In addition store V(f) in the group on the **left wire occurrences** with one relation for each private left vertex equating its ordered input and output products. There is no relation on a shared vertex. For a 3-arrow require the W-equations and unchanged V-group elements. Juxtaposition includes the indexed groups; sequential gluing identifies persisting wires and concatenates their two records. These maps respect all private relations. The W-equations compose by concatenating move words in reverse execution order, and V-equality composes by group multiplication. Signed swap transports record a generator on each of their two wires and its inverse on reversal. Normalize the shuffle boundaries as in Response 198. A private prism preserves V in the group by exactly its private relation. This interprets the full surface by the identity-square and endomorphism test of Response 19.

Suppose a surface filler exists. Then the W-divisions succeed. Replay as above. The resulting raw reading and the target now have identical W-words, and for each f their two V-words represent the same element of the left group. They have exactly the same set of letters since every (e,f) is read on both wires. That set is an antichain in the directed private wiring: f cannot cross a wire and then a private descendant of that wire. After its first crossing the wire is strictly to the left of f; while f is live, a private step consuming it lies entirely to the left and leaves all descendants there. If the descendant were crossed first, its ancestor would already have been consumed.

Any such antichain embeds as independent free generators in the left group. Cut the private wiring at all shared ports. Take a joint time cut through the selected private-network wires by placing all their producers and their predecessors before the cut and all their consumers after it. These requirements are compatible by the antichain condition. Assign distinct free generators to the selected wires and identity to every other wire in that cut. Extend backwards: put the ordered product of the assigned outputs of a private vertex on its first input and identity on the remaining inputs. Extend forwards by putting the ordered input product on its first output and identity on the other outputs. All these first ports exist; each wire has at most one creator and consumer. At free ends no relation is imposed. This supplies a group homomorphism which reads the two V-words as literal positive words on freely independent letters. Their equality in the model therefore implies their literal equality in the algorithm. This proves necessity without a word-problem oracle.

At five the private move words are forced by the W-divisions and all simultaneous distinct native prism steps commute by the disjoint-window argument of Response 195. Thus parallel strict prism pastes coincide. There are no higher generators in the strict hom. Apply [positive attachment lifting](#researcher-response-8) at the old written faces, and the elementary return test in degree three as before.

**Reproduction.** Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_total_ports.py`. It checks 79,399 ordered comparisons on 4,941 raw histories against directed prism reachability and tests all 28 simultaneous prism pairs found. The cases include left-to-right and right-to-left transfers, right-only long rules, and private left splits. The solver checks contiguity on the actual right wire during every replay. Use `--query FILE` in the [wire-word format](#researcher-response-198), with nonempty total sides. Generate `--agda-dir DIR` and run `agda --safe -i src -i DIR DIR/SharedWireTransfers.agda` for the fully conservative example with two-way column transfers, private splitting and all elementary returns. Agda 2.8.0 accepted the context. [Joint-port solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_total_ports.py)

## Researcher Response 201

**At each given old degree-four judgment of a finite positive Gray 3-computad with no spatial triple, surface inhabitation is decidable.** This includes the incomparable faces left open by Response 19. For explicit positioned histories and polygon readings the four binary surfaces containing interchange have the same answer, computable in polynomial space. There is no restriction on the spatial support of a polygon relative to its own internal events, on the number of private or shared rules, or on changes of spatial path length. With the raw decision of Response 18 this decides whether the given judgment witnesses a failure. The quantifier here is over a *specified judgment*; iterating this test is not a decision of the universal context condition.

### A signed fixed hom at degree four

Use the strict readings of Response 8. In each fixed hom allow the elementary interval squares in both directions, keeping every named polygon directed. Take diagrams modulo the ordinary strict fixed-hom laws and cancellation of inverse squares. The pure signed square groupoid on temporal histories is thin by the disjoint sorting diamonds of Response 9. Identify histories in a component and transport diagram ends along its unique arrows. At the next local degree put one arrow from one such diagram to another exactly when a succession of directed native mixed prisms in signed contexts connects them. This relation is closed under all fixed-hom compositions: pad with identities and perform the two successions in order. Take identities in higher degrees.

These fixed homs assemble to a strict Gray-enriched interpretation. Exterior path actions extend to signed diagrams, since they preserve swaps, disjointness and prism signs. If two spatially composable homs both admit an event, neither admits a pair of spatially composable events at its poles. Thus, in these two input homs, histories are literal, diagrams are the original directed polygon diagrams, and all higher arrows are identities. Use the usual strict tensor composition there followed by the target hom map. Its mixed degree-three generators are the stipulated prism inequalities, and its degree-four generators land in identities by uniqueness of parallel local 3-arrows. If one factor admits no event, positivity leaves only exterior path actions from that factor. For three composable factors at least one has only stationary paths. The associativity check therefore reduces to the compatibility of the original tensor composition with exterior path actions, or to concatenating those paths. The unit is the empty exterior path. Every spatial square on lists is an identity after transport; Response 19 (or the criterion of Response 179) interprets the full binary surface. Hence any surface filler implies signed reachability at its strict readings.

Conversely, interpret a signed square by a chosen weak inverse to the native square in the interchange surface, available with its cancellation cells by Response 98. Commutations of disjoint temporal steps have invertible coherence in the ordinary weak fixed hom, and both directions of a dipole cancellation have fillers. Consequently every equality used for signed diagrams can be realized by an equivalence at the next degree. End transports introduce only such cancellable pairs at a matched seam. A forward prism is realized by its native cell, also in any composite of signed steps. Pasting these realizations yields the requested surface filler: realize the positive parts at their strict readings by the prescribed-boundary comparison of Response 8; different positive writings of the same strict diagram are equivalent there, so one can attach the two original faces. Equivalently one may first adjoin formal reversed square generators to the positive fixed-hom presentation, realize its ordinary strict commutations by ordinary computad comparison, then interpret those generators and the two cancellation witnesses in the surface. This proves sufficiency already for interchange alone.

### Finite graph for the comparison

Between two successive named polygon occurrences, any signed square string is determined by its ends. A vertex records each named occurrence in temporal execution order, its entire literal history just before execution, its rule index and its start position in that history. The literal initial and final histories of the judgment are fixed. Consecutive records determine the two ends of their signed connector, including at those two outer boundaries. Start the search at the records of the first face. Its elementary updates are as follows.

1. Commute a signed adjacent swap on a disjoint temporal window past one polygon. Change its recorded history by that swap on either side of the window.
2. Exchange consecutive polygons on disjoint temporal windows when the first output history is literally the second recorded history.
3. Move one polygon one position later across a neighboring event spatially disjoint from the polygon's **whole** declared window. Pass the event across its input block by swaps to obtain the new recorded history. Test spatial disjointness on the path after the input block, using the final spatial path of that window. This checks both spatial orders, including for length-changing events. Response 18 gives the same temporal direction in both orders.

The first two updates are reversible. Every update preserves the existence of all connectors. To see completeness, expand a strict diagram equality into dipole cancellations and exchanges of elementary steps on disjoint temporal windows. With no polygon the records stay fixed. With one or two polygons the exchange gives exactly the first or second update. If an expansion needs a different pure connector at fixed ends, thinness makes it the same connector. For a prism in context, serialize the other factors to a common prefix and suffix of elementary steps using ordinary fixed-hom interchange. On its characteristic negative face the polygon is immediately before the disjoint event at the recorded step. On the positive face it is immediately after it. The other steps of these two faces are pure swaps within the characteristic blocks. Conversely these two faces fit at every instance of update 3 by pure signed transport at both ends. This gives exactly the reachability relation used in the model.

Named multiplicities must agree. If their sum is m, an intermediate history has length at most the initial temporal length plus m times the maximum positive temporal growth of one rule (or zero if none grow). Along such a history the underlying spatial path grows by at most its length times the maximum positive spatial growth of one 2-generator. A record list therefore occupies polynomial space in the explicit inputs. There are at most exponentially many lists in a polynomial number of bits. Guess a path up to that bound using one list and a counter, and apply NPSPACE = PSPACE. This complexity bound is for readings as input. The executable below uses exhaustive breadth-first search and also gives a sequence of move kinds for positive answers.

**Reproduction.** Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_signed_width_two.py`. It compares 1,085 ordered queries with the independent incidence solver of Response 197, visiting 1,754 descriptions. Seven further queries use changing spatial lengths and whole-window rules. In particular, declaring a split on the left edge permits its forward prism past the right event; giving the same internal split the full two-edge window makes both directions between the corresponding readings fail. For `--query FILE`, supply JSON fields `edges` (one-character edge names to object pairs), `marks` (event names to spatial path pairs), `rules` (objects with `path`, `source`, `target`), `start` (edge path), `source` (initial history), and `first`, `second` (the two raw readings). A positioned event is `[offset,mark]`; a reading step is `[zero_based_rule_index,position]` or `["swap",position]`. [Signed degree-four solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_signed_width_two.py)

## Researcher Response 202

**Every finite width in the ordinary insertion filtration has decidable conversion and type checking, with unrestricted pruning.** Moreover the least uniform width for inserting an individual tree $T$ is exactly $\dim T-t(T)$, where $t(T)$ is its unary trunk length. At a scalar specialization the least width can drop, and the surviving positions give an exact formula below. These results let one test whether a *specified witness* for Q1 actually uses the width at which it was found. They also give principal finite raw contexts for testing reflection at each width, with a decidable test for eliminating cases that already type at the preceding width.

Allowing empty strings in the chart proof would require a different lifting theorem. Take one 2-bead with both of its 1-seams empty. Both seams evaluate to the identity on the same vertex. Its representing raw computad is exactly $(x,a:1_x\to1_x)$. The projection to its free strict category fails prescribed-boundary lifting at the diagonal braid and the identity in degree four. Thus the chart projection used for nonempty strings cannot justify adding pruning. The normalization argument instead treats pruning as a rule from the beginning. [Positive chart comparison](#researcher-response-199) · [Scalar raw obstruction](#researcher-response-1)

### Normalization with the width test

Write $w(T)=\dim T-t(T)$. Present $B_b$ by all published insertion instances with $w(T)\le b$, together with disc and endo removal, using [Response 196](#researcher-response-196). In the published oriented reduction retain every identity insertion. For insertion of a standard composite retain exactly those redexes whose inner arity satisfies $w(T)\le b$. Keep the original branch-height test, the exclusions for identity and disc heads, and reduction in arguments and generic head types. Restricting a confluent relation need not preserve confluence, so we verify the joins.

First, suspension preserves width. Signed truncation at height $s$ has height $\min(s,\dim T)$ and retains at least $\min(s,t(T))$ unary edges. In particular every signed restriction of an allowed insertion either acts identically or inserts another allowed tree. Exterior substitutions are independent of the bound. They send the selected peak to the embedded standard term and fix the other peaks at their retained coordinates. The recursive typing of standard boundaries uses only the indicated signed restrictions. Joined labellings agree with the original labellings on maximal coordinates after composition with the exterior and interior; equality on other coordinates follows from their globular types. These verifications give the same support, conversion, substitution and suspension conditions in the restricted theory. In particular when a standard head transported along an allowed exterior must reduce to the new standard head, the induction on its two signed faces uses only allowed insertions. The disc and identity cases use disc and endo removal. [Finster–Rice–Vicary, §§3.2–3.3, Theorem 30 and Lemmas 44–49](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303#page=19)

The symmetric closure of reduction, with transitivity and reflexivity, gives exactly $B_b$ equality. In the direction from equations to reductions the published proof first handles a padded inner standard term by endo removal and insertion of an identity disc. Induction removes the excess height until it can insert the original $T$. The extra discs have width zero. At an outer disc or identity, the comparison uses the same exterior on a standard type, as checked above. The bounded-equality induction for comparing the nonmaximal entries of substitutions uses the faces of the agreed maximal entries in the *restricted* theory. These are the ingredients of Lemma 33 and Proposition 38; none requires a larger inner tree. Termination follows since each oriented step is a published reduction. [Reduction and equality](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303#page=22)

For the nested critical pair, suppose $T$ was to be inserted at an outer peak, and $U$ can first be inserted into $T$ at $Q$. Joining after doing the inner step requires inserting $T'=T\ll_Q U$ into the original outer tree. Its height is at most that of $T$: the new column reaches no further than the leaf it replaces. If $T$ is nonlinear its trunk cannot shorten. Any branch eligible for replacement starts at or below the first non-unary node, since a child strictly above that node has a nonlinear subtree. If $T$ is linear the joined tree is $U$ itself. Hence $w(T')\le b$ whenever both initial insertions were allowed. On the other side of the square the residual inserts $U$ itself. The residual branch address, the joined substitutions and the exterior comparison are the ones of Lemma 52. At the changed maximal entry the comparison is precisely standard-term transport along the $U$-exterior, already proved within the bound. The remaining discrepancies are lower-dimensional equalities in $B_b$.

For distinct outer peaks the residual insertions use the same two inner trees, and the two orders of joining agree on the maximal entries. Two presentations of the same peak likewise agree there. A reduction inside the labels or the bound type commutes with reindexing by the same exterior; if this exposes an identity or a disc, use its removal and standard-boundary transport. The disc and endo overlaps that contain no insertion use only their respective removal rules and matching reductions of their subterms. Thus the induction of Theorem 43 on dimension and subterms joins every restricted critical pair: when it appeals to lower-dimensional equality, the preceding comparisons exhibit that equality at the same width. Termination and local confluence give a unique normal form $N_b$. Normalizing the finitely many type comparisons in a typing derivation now decides typing, including for nonglobular computads and converted intermediate expressions. [Critical pairs, particularly Lemmas 50–60](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303#page=29)

### The least width for one insertion

Fix a nonlinear tree $T$ of height $d$ and trunk $j$. Take the ordinary binary arity $S=D^d\vee_jD^d$. In its first slot insert $T$ and call the joined arity $J$. Compare the nested standard binary head under the generic exterior with the head on $J$ at the **transported** bound type, using the variable tuple. These are raw terms of the same literal type. For $b<d-j$, the first slot's standard term on $T$ is normal on its variable labelling and cannot be inserted. The other slot is a variable. The nested normal form therefore retains outer arity $S$. On the joined side only the generic bound type could change: the labels are variables and the two generic strict faces of the top operation on $J$ are distinct. Neither outer tree is linear. The second normal form consequently has outer arity $J$, which has strictly more edges than $S$ because $T$ has more than $d$ edges. Normalization proves inequality. At width $d-j$ the one generic insertion suffices. This proves sharpness for **each tree individually**, even if only one of its branches has maximum height. A disc costs zero. One can also fold every rank-$r$ variable to $g_r$ in the raw loop tower $g_r:g_{r-1}\to g_{r-1}$ on one object $g_0$. Every label of the generic arity is still a variable and the same two outer arities survive.

Now take one $d$-scalar $a$ at the iterated identity on $x$. Keep the outside $d$-slot labelled by $a$. Within $T$ choose any subset $M$ of its depth-$d$ positions, put $a$ on those and the identity on the others, and give all lower-dimensional variables their iterated identity values. For $|M|\ge2$ the least width equating the two raw terms is
$$
d-\operatorname{length}(\text{longest common address prefix of the positions in }M).
$$
For zero or one selected position the least width is zero.

Indeed prune each unselected tip, including original shorter tips, until only paths to selected positions remain in the inserted window. For nonempty $M$ this leaves the tree $T_M$ of their prefixes. Every such pruning factors the scalar tuple through the pruned arity; signed-boundary transport identifies the old standard term there with the new one already under strict units. Consequently the two sides become the generic comparison for $T_M$ at the **original cut $j$**, specialized to the surviving scalar labels. For the joined head this follows on its generic bound type by composing the pruning maps with the original exterior. On the selected coordinate their composite sends the peak to the standard term of $T_M$; on all the other peaks it preserves the retained positions. This identifies the transported types before specializing. The new trunk is at least $j$, so insertion at that cut is admissible. For two or more survivors all maximal labels are now variables. No further pruning occurs. Below $w(T_M)$ the same different outer arities persist in the two normal forms; at $w(T_M)$ the direct rule applies. A single path is a disc. If there are no survivors, prune the whole window down to its stationary seam: the selected slot on the nested side is an identity tower on that seam and is pruned to the same surviving outside disc. Its generic operation is the standard one there by strict-unit standard-boundary transport. This proves the formula, including the fully empty input. For instance, for a tree with one short 1-column followed by a column with two successive 2-cells the loop tower requires width two, while retaining both top slots on a scalar requires only width one.

### Consequence for old-boundary reflection

The tameness and support checks above and the presence of all three strict-unit rules give Rice's rehydration theorem on pasting contexts separately for each $B_b$. Its equalities can be checked with $N_b$. The exact-class fitting criterion of Response 27 therefore applies with this same normal form. In particular on globular generating data the raw representatives can be fitted at every compatible prescribed raw boundary: lift a raw pair at its common strict positional value to the pasting tree, use commutation of $N_b$ with variable relabelling and positional uniqueness to get equality upstairs, then specialize its full-support, identity-class comparison. The fitting steps use only strict units. This part applies to globular presentations with repeated labels as well as to trees. [Rice, Theorem 4.5.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17068#page=193) · [Positional comparison and fitting](#researcher-response-27)

For arbitrary raw attachments, fix the literal old type and a *normal witness writing* at width $b$. Form its terminal-computad shape $s$ and principal finite raw context $D_s^b$ by the occurrence identifications of Response 34, now replaying $N_b$ in its typing comparisons. Normalizing still commutes with every generator-preserving relabelling, since the additional test uses only the generic inner tree. Thus the maps from $D_s^b$ into $X$ classify exactly these marked realizations. There is also an effective narrower-width test on this entire family. Keep the writing fixed and run its typing check at $c<b$ on the terminal shape. If it fails, no realization checks at $c$, by relabelling to the terminal computad. If it succeeds, trace the additional comparisons with the same placeholders. Close the resulting identifications under their raw declarations. This gives one quotient of $D_s^b$ through which a realizing map factors exactly when the writing types at $c$. In fact a $b$-normal writing stays $c$-normal whenever it checks there, since the directed reductions form nested subsets. At output degree $q$, all widths at least $q-1$ give the same typing test on a fixed writing at a raw type, by the dimension bound of Response 196. A least-width failure can therefore be sought just among the principal contexts where the writing fails the preceding-width test at the generic assignment. Existence of a *different* raw inhabitant in those contexts is still the test required by Q1.
